about: The round-11 daily-loop evaluation's demo world (four courses) at four checkpoints: seed, 8 Nov after the seeded study; lesson-review, 9 Nov after the Linear Algebra review; day-done, the end of 9 Nov, when every item its plan held was done; day-after, the end of 10 Nov, unchanged through 17 Nov. Calculus I and Real Analysis are the same at every one.

points: Identifies $X \sim \text{Bin}(n,p)$: fixed $n$, independent trials, constant $p$, counting successes
$p^k(1-p)^{n-k}$ is the probability of one specific arrangement
$\binom{n}{k}$ counts the disjoint arrangements, so their probabilities add
review.prompt: Each of $n$ independent trials succeeds with probability $p$ (give concrete numbers, e.g. $n=8$, $p=0.4$, exactly $3$ successes). Ask for the probability as an expression with its reason. Tests whether he includes $\binom{n}{k}$ and can say what it counts.

points: Counts over equally likely outcomes (ordered) or uses $P(X\le k)$ differences
